subject.title: fix(markdown-core): guard against NaN in ordered list start attribute

question: Should markdown-core normalize malformed markdown-it ordered-list tokens when no supported OpenClaw path to such tokens has been demonstrated?
rationale: The code change is mechanically safe, but repository policy distinguishes observed malformed input from hypothetical internal states, and the submitted evidence does not establish which category this case belongs to.

options.title: Require reachable proof
options.body: Ask for an actual before-and-after reproduction through `markdownToIR` or an existing token-extension boundary, with a test that fails on current main.

options.title: Accept defensive hardening
options.body: Merge the fallback as intentional defense in depth after replacing the current tests with focused coverage of the malformed token value.

recommendation.title: Require reachable proof
recommendation.body: Ask for an actual before-and-after reproduction through `markdownToIR` or an existing token-extension boundary, with a test that fails on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is primarily whether this defensive branch fits the repository’s lean-core and realistic-input policy.
